newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-ARGENTINA SCORE MODEST WIN OVER VENEZUELA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINA SCORE MODEST WIN OVER VENEZUELA.

text.p: Argentina had to be content with a modest 2-0 win over Venezuela, the team with the leakiest defence in South America, in their World Cup qualifier on Sunday.
The result -- Argentina's fourth successive win in the qualifying tournament -- left the two-time world champions all but mathematically certain of a place in France next year.
But the final score was a disappointment to the capacity crowd at the River Plate stadium, who had been expecting a hatful of goals against a team that has conceeded 34 in their previous 12 games.
Hernan Crespo opened the scoring after half an hour, just as the crowd was begining to get on Argentina's backs, and substitute Pablo Paz headed the second eleven minutes into the second half.
Crespo's goal partially compensated Argentina coach Daniel Passarella for the abuse he has received for keeping the striker in the team at the expense of Gabriel Batistuta.
Argentina dominated the game from start to finish but they were defied time and again by world class goalkeeping from Rafael Dudamel.

Dudamel, however, had no chance when Crespo, receiving possibly the only accurate pass his striking partner Claudio Lopez managed in the entire game, beat a defender and scored from close range in the 30th minute.
Venezuela's also defenders cleared two balls off the goal-line before halftime and survived a penalty claim when Javier Zanetti went tumbling over in the area.
Argentina goalkeeper Carlos Roa made his only difficult save of the game one minute after Crespo's goal, tipping a curling free kick by Gabriel Miranda over the crossbar.
Paz came on when central defender Roberto Ayala was injured in the 49th minute and seven minutes later rose to head Marcelo Gallardo's cross into the net.
Shortly afterward, Dudamel produced his best save of the day when he blocked a drive by Lopez at almost point-blank range.
Argentina playmaker Ariel Ortega, who has been out of action for the last month with a knee injury, replaced Gallardo for the last half an hour.
Despite facing modest opposition, Argentina also showed the side of the game that has made them unpopular among many fans.
Gallardo showed have been booked for attempting to win a penalty with a blatant dive in the first half while the Venezuelan players were victims of numerous rash challenges.

Argentina: 1-Carlos Roa, 2-Roberto Ayala (Pablo Paz 49, 6-Roberto Sensini, 3-Jose Chamot, 4-Javier Zanetti, 5-Leonardo Astrada, 8-Diego Simeone, 11-Sebastin Veron, 10-Marcelo Gallardo (19-Ariel Ortega, 57); 7-Claudio Lopez, (20-Sergio Berti, 77), 9-Hernan Crespo.

Venezuela: 1-Rafael Dudamel, 2-David Macintosh, 3-Alexander Echenique, 4-Jose Manuel Rey, 15-Elvis Martinez, 6-Leonardo Gonzalez, 7-Robert Moran (13-Johnny Lucena, 71), 8-Gerson Diaz (13-Osvaldo Palencia, 75), 9-Giovanni Savarese, 10-Gabriel Miranda 16-Robert Rodallega.
